findings.title: A device rejected at the limit is accepted on its next request
findings.body: tagDeviceUI adds the device ID to the 29-minute local cache before persisting it. When CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, this new return propagates the error for the first request but does not remove that cache entry. A retry for the same device then hits the cache, skips the database limit check, returns nil from TagDevice, and receives an anonymous identity even though the limit remains full. Only cache a device after a successful store operation, or invalidate the cache entry on every store error.

findings.title: The count-and-insert limit check is not atomic
findings.body: CountDevices is performed in one database session and the subsequent upsert is performed later in another session, without a transaction or lock. If the count is one below the limit, multiple concurrent requests with distinct device IDs can all observe available capacity and all insert successfully, exceeding the configured limit by an arbitrary number of concurrent requests. The admission check and creation need serialization/locking or a database-enforced quota mechanism.

findings.title: Anonymous callers can bypass the device limit by omitting the device header
findings.body: TagDevice returns success immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent, and Authenticate treats that success as permission to create an anonymous identity. Because this is a caller-controlled HTTP header, a client can simply omit it and never reach the count or limit check. Thus device_limit only restricts cooperative clients and cannot enforce a limit on anonymous access unless missing or unverifiable device identifiers are handled explicitly.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication now waits indefinitely for device-store operations
findings.body: Authentication now invokes TagDevice synchronously using the request context. The removed implementation ran this work asynchronously with an explicit two-minute timeout; the supplied request context need not have any deadline. On a slow database, connection-pool exhaustion, or a stalled query, each cache-miss anonymous authentication can block until the client disconnects or the database returns, causing anonymous request latency and potential request exhaustion even when device_limit is disabled. Preserve a bounded context for the store operation while retaining the synchronous limit decision.
